Answers:

**h01.** `s3presign.Runner` (S3 presigned-URL refresher, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`) — refreshes attachment `reference` URLs whose presign is within 4 days of its 5-day expiry (`runner.go:85-91`) — **every 12 hours** (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`; ticker loop `runner.go:29-41`) — wired in `Server.startBackgroundRunners`: eager `RunOnce` at `server/server.go:163`, then `go s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` at `server/server.go:169` (called from `Server.Start`, `server/server.go:129`).

**h02.** Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual HTTP send at `webhook.go:152` via `safeClient.Do`); async entry `webhook.PostAsync` (`webhook.go:184`) feeds a 128-slot queue drained by 4 goroutines (`webhook.go:39-55`).
Protection: two layers — (1) dial-time SSRF guard `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`) installed as the shared client's `Transport.DialContext` (`webhook.go:32-37`), rejecting resolved IPs in reserved ranges via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:44-54`, CIDR list `validate.go:14-23` incl. 127/8, RFC-1918, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10); this also defeats DNS rebinding. (2) Up-front `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) called at webhook create/update (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`). Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`).

**h03.** Abstraction package: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:3` — `IdentityProviderUserInfo`, the shared provider-neutral user-info contract). Implementation package: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:19` `IdentityProvider`, `NewIdentityProvider` at `:26`, `ExchangeToken` at `:45`). OAuth2 (with PKCE support) is the only concrete protocol shipped; consumed at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:12-13`.

**h04.** **No.** `mysql.NewDB` (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20`) is referenced exactly once outside its own package — the factory `NewDBDriver` at `store/db/db.go:22`. A repo-wide grep for `mysql.NewDB(`/`NewDB(` yields only `store/db/db.go:20,22,24` plus the three declarations; the only other `store/db/mysql` import is `store/db/db.go:8`. (The `mysql.*` hits in `store/test/containers.go:101-105` are the TestContainers `modules/mysql` package, not this driver. Tests that construct a driver directly use `sqlite.NewDB` — `store/demo_seed_test.go:24`, `store/deployment_config_test.go:416`.)

**h05.** Mechanism: **explicit Go code**, per driver, inside the delete-user transaction — not a DB-level cascade.
- `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = ?`): `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:400-402`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:437-439`, `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:400-402`; invoked from `deleteUserTargetsTx` (`store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:102` and peers).
- Reactions *on* the user's memos are also removed by content id: `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:380-388` (called at `:99`).
- Evidence it is not DB-level: the `reaction` tables declare no foreign keys — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`. The only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the whole schema is `memo_share.memo_id → memo.id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109` and peers).
- Entry point: `Store.DeleteUser` → `s.driver.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171-172`).

**h06.** Handlers (all `*APIV1Service`):
- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` (`:157`)
- `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (`:513`)
- `DeleteMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518` → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (`:562`)
- `CreateMemoComment` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20` → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (`:119`)
- `SetMemoAttachments` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:16` (`:48`)
- `SetMemoRelations` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:16` (`:48`)

Convergence: `webhook.PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` (every path enqueues here, via `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`, `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:71`, or `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook`, `:43`), which the worker pool hands to `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`) for the actual send.

**h07.** Route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124`):
- `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168`
- `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715`
- `Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go:148` (checks `userCache` only when finding by ID; a username lookup falls through)
- `Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go:136` → `s.driver.ListUsers` (interface, `store/driver.go:47`)
- `sqlite.DB.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88` (default driver; MySQL/Postgres peers otherwise)
- Back in the handler: `parseDataURI` decodes the stored base64 data-URI in `user.AvatarURL` and it is written with `c.Blob` (`fileserver.go:196-209`); MIME is restricted by `avatarAllowedTypes` (`fileserver.go:75`).

**h08.** Two declarers:
- `*s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` — **invoked** — callers: `Server.startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go:163`) and `s3presign.Runner.Run` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36`).
- `*memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` — **not invoked** (dead in production and in tests). The only production use of that package is the free function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447`); `memopayload.NewRunner` has no callers at all.

**h09.** Count: **8** declarations in the Go backend, 6 of them non-test.
Non-test declarers: `*store.Store` (`store/store.go:72`), `*cache.Cache` (`store/cache/cache.go:187`), `*sqlite.DB` (`store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`), `*mysql.DB` (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`), `*postgres.DB` (`store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`), `*apiv1.SSEHub` (`server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`). Test-only: `MemoFilterTestContext` and `AttachmentFilterTestContext` (`store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200`, `:282`).
Actually called by non-test server code:
- `Store.Close` ← `Server.Shutdown`, `server/server.go:146`
- `SSEHub.Close` ← `Server.closeLongLivedConnections`, `server/server.go:206`
- `Cache.Close` (×3 instances) ← `Store.Close`, `store/store.go:74-76`
- `Driver.Close` → the sqlite/mysql/postgres `DB.Close` ← `Store.Close`, `store/store.go:78` (only the driver selected by `db.NewDBDriver` actually runs; sqlite by default)

**h10.** `(*conditionRenderer).addArg` — `internal/filter/render.go` (declared at `internal/filter/render.go:171`; used at `:213`, `:287`, `:329`, …) — approx fan-in **~14 distinct calling functions / ~28 call sites**, all production code. (Runner-up by raw graph count is `filter.NewEngine`, `internal/filter/engine.go:24`, at 32 — but 29 of those callers are `_test.go` files; only 3 are production.)

**h11.** 1st: **`store.User`** (`store/user.go`) — ~6 non-test packages outside `store/`: `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/rss`.
2nd: **`store.Memo`** (`store/memo.go`) — ~4: `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`.
(Next: `store.Attachment` at ~3. Counts exclude the sibling driver packages `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}`, which reference all of them.)

**h12.** Concrete method: **`(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo`** — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16`; the `INSERT INTO \`memo\` … RETURNING …` statement is built at `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:40` and executed at `:41`.
Determination: the driver is chosen at startup, not at the call site. `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` and the `--driver` flag default (`cmd/memos/main.go:122`, `:130`) set `Profile.Driver` (`cmd/memos/main.go:43`); `db.NewDBDriver` switches on it and returns `sqlite.NewDB` (`store/db/db.go:16-26`, sqlite branch `:20`); that value is stored as `Store.driver` via `store.New` (`cmd/memos/main.go:57,64`). `Store.CreateMemo` validates the UID then delegates through the `store.Driver` interface (`store/memo.go:109-114`), so with no flags the sqlite implementation is the only one reachable.

**h13.** Implementation: the unexported `markdown.service` struct — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:57` (the sole implementer of `markdown.Service`, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`; `ExtractAll` at `:356`). No mock/alternate implementation exists in the repo.
Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:84`; called once in production at `NewAPIV1Service`, `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51`, with `WithTagExtension()` + `WithMentionExtension()`. (Test-only second construction: `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`.)
Holders of the interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`); `RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`), injected from the API service at `server/server.go:85`; `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`, never constructed in production) and the `markdownService markdown.Service` parameter of `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`).

**h14.** Computation site: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, which delegates to `service.ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`) for a single-pass goldmark walk.
Triggers: `CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`, before the INSERT) and `UpdateMemo` only when the `content` field is in the update mask (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, guarded by `:436-437`). A bulk backfill path exists in `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-71`) but is not wired into startup (see h08).
Extracted into `memo.Payload`: `Tags` (all `#tag`s) and `Property` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:84-85`) — the property struct carries `Title` (first heading text), `HasLink`, `HasCode`, `HasTaskList`, `HasIncompleteTasks` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:387-404`; equivalent single-purpose path at `:217-226`).

**h15.** Enforcement sites:
- `APIV1Service.checkMemoReadAccess` (archived→creator-only; non-public requires auth; private→creator only) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-68`, used by `GetMemo` (`:356`, `:367`) and `ListMemoComments` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:148`)
- `ListMemos` query-scoping (anonymous → `PUBLIC`; other user's memos → `PUBLIC`+`PROTECTED`; own → CEL filter) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227`
- `FileServerService.checkAttachmentPermission` (public+anonymous-allowed pass, share-token fallback, private→creator/admin) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650-703`
- `UpsertMemoReaction` / `DeleteMemoReaction` visibility gate — `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30-40` and `:83`
- `CreateMemoComment` parent-memo gate — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41` (plus comment-visibility constraint at `:100`)
- `SetMemoAttachments` gate — `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214-222`; attachment-level gate — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:445-451`
- User stats scoping — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84-90` and `:218-220`
- RSS feeds restricted to `PUBLIC` — `server/router/rss/rss.go:90` (explore) and `:141` (per-user)
- Sitemap restricted to `PUBLIC` — `server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150`
- Mention/notification eligibility — `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62-84`; email notification gating — `server/notification/email.go:313-316`

**r01.** Premise is wrong on both counts: **there is no Redis anywhere in this repo** (no `redis` import, dependency, or config — repo-wide grep returns zero hits), and there is no per-entry TTL specific to users. Actual mechanism: a process-local in-memory cache, `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` type, `cache.New` at `:59`-region, `Config` at `:43`). `store.New` builds three of them — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — from one shared `cache.Config`: `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000` (`store/store.go:39-53`). So user entries live 10 minutes, swept every 5 minutes; `Cache.Set` applies `DefaultTTL` (`store/cache/cache.go:94`). Users are cached on read/list (`store/user.go:143`, `:167`) and evicted on delete (`store/user_delete.go:39-41`).

**r02.** Premise is wrong: **there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase** — no limiter registration, no per-user quotas, no `golang.org/x/time/rate` or Echo rate-limit middleware (repo-wide case-insensitive grep for rate-limit yields only a comment aspiration in `internal/email/doc.go:86`). The middleware actually registered is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`), static/SPA serving (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54,59`), gRPC-Gateway auth middleware (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69-96`), and Connect interceptors: Metadata, Logging, Recovery (`server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go:22,98,164`). The only request-concurrency limits are semaphores for thumbnail/image work (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:46-47`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:116`).

**r03.** Premise is wrong: **no nightly database-cleanup job is scheduled — none exists.** A generic cron scheduler package ships (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `ParseCronExpression` at `internal/scheduler/parser.go:28`), but it is never instantiated in production code: every `scheduler.New(...)` / `Register(...)` call site is a test or example (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `integration_test.go`), and `server/server.go` imports it nowhere. The only real background work is the 12-hour S3 presign refresher started in `Server.startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go:153-174`), which uses a `time.Ticker`, not cron, and does no cleanup.

**r04.** Premise is wrong: **there is no message broker at all** — neither NATS nor RabbitMQ (nor Kafka/AMQP) appears in `go.mod` or any Go source, and no queue is declared anywhere. Actual mechanism: an in-process buffered Go channel. `asyncPostQueue` is a `chan *WebhookRequestPayload` with capacity 128 (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by 4 goroutines started in `package init` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `Post` (`:120`). Producers use `PostAsync` (`:184`), which drops the delivery with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`). Consequence: deliveries are best-effort, in-memory, and lost on restart — no persistence, no retry.

**r05.** Premise is wrong: **there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server in this repo** (no `graphql` dependency in `go.mod`, no `.graphql`/`.gql` files, no resolver code). The public API surface is Protobuf-defined RPC: `.proto` files under `proto/` generating `proto/gen/` (Go + OpenAPI) and `web/src/types/proto/` (TypeScript), served two ways from one service implementation — Connect RPC handlers and a gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON mux, both registered in `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65-110`, e.g. `RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer` at `:107`), wired at `server/server.go:88`. Additional non-RPC surfaces: HTTP file server `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go:67`), MCP (`server/server.go:92-96`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`). Endpoint access policy lives in `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`, not a schema.
